title: Shrimp and noodles with cheese sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp and noodles with cheese sauce is a dish that combines seafood, pasta and a creamy cheese‑based sauce. The shrimp cook quickly, while the noodles (usually egg noodles or spaghetti) soak up the flavorful sauce, creating a hearty and aromatic meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The shrimp‑and‑cheese combination is popular in Asian‑European fusion cuisine, where creamy sauces are used to mellow the taste of seafood.
Shrimp are high‑protein and low‑calorie, making the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.
The cheese sauce can be made from various cheeses: cheddar, parmesan, mozzarella or cream cheese, each giving a distinct flavor profile.
Traditionally the noodles are cooked al dente to retain texture and avoid turning mushy in the sauce.
Quick sauté of shrimp until pink preserves their tenderness and prevents overcooking.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat dishes, shrimp contain little saturated fat, supporting heart‑healthy eating.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Shrimp are a good source of selenium, zinc and iodine, which support immune function and thyroid health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Balanced carbohydrates
items.content: The noodles supply energy, and the protein‑carb pairing helps moderate blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people monitoring their cholesterol should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Cheese sauces are often salty; those with hypertension should reduce added salt or use low‑sodium cheese.

items.title: Additives in prepared sauces
items.content: Store‑bought sauces may contain preservatives and flavor enhancers; homemade sauce is preferable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, garnished with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill and a wedge of lemon. Add vegetables like broccoli, peas or bell pepper for extra volume and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. When reheating, stir in a splash of milk or cream to restore the sauce’s creamy texture.
